gap: No result ChatGPT got lines the products up by what ONE extra battery actually gives you (the shopper's case) on a common cycle-life basis: EcoFlow DELTA 3 / 3 Plus and Anker C1000X go to about 2.1 kWh in 1 kWh steps, the DJI Power 1000 V2 jumps to 3,072 Wh because its smallest pack is 2,048 Wh, and the advertised maximums (5 kWh, 11 kWh) depend on different pack sizes and counts. EcoFlow's 5 kWh needs the 4,096 Wh DELTA Pro 3 extra battery on an adapter cable.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), BatteryRank (cited), Off Grid Field Guide (cited) and WattHourLab (cited). Off Grid Field Guide already warns that 'makers rate cycle life to different end points' and gives Jackery 4,000 to 70%, Anker 3,000 to 80% and EcoFlow DELTA 3 4,000 to 80%, so the cycle-life part of the normalisation is taken. BatteryRank already caps the DELTA 3 Plus at one DELTA 3 pack (2,048 Wh). StormWatts lists the 4,096 Wh DELTA Pro 3 extra battery and the XT150 cable but never shows how 5 kWh adds up. None of them puts 'total after one extra battery' and 'smallest add-on step' in one column across EcoFlow, Anker, DJI, Jackery HomePower and OUPES, so the new part is that table and its footnote.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's EcoFlow DELTA 3 pick for a shopper who wants to go from 1 kWh to 2 kWh: it has the smallest step (1,024 Wh) and the same 80% end point as DJI and Anker. The '~5 kWh' in ChatGPT's table is misleading for an add-one-battery buyer, because one DELTA 3 pack stops at 2,048 Wh. For a bigger single jump, the DJI Power 1000 V2 reaches 3,072 Wh with one pack at 4,000 cycles to 80%. DJI's US product URLs redirected to a 404 page on 2026-11-08, so that route needs a US availability check before anyone recommends it.

findings.label: Cycle life
findings.note: DJI's wording: 'Maintains over 80% capacity after 4000 cycles.' The same page lists 1,024 Wh and about 14.2 kg, and the 100–120 V model DYM1000V2L at 20 A max. https://www.dji.com/power-1000-v2 and /specs both redirected to a DJI 404 page on 2026-11-08.

findings.label: Pack size, count and cycle rating
findings.value: about 2 kWh per pack (2,048 Wh), up to 5 packs, 'up to 4000 cycles' with no end % given
findings.source_title: The DJI Power Expansion Battery 2000 Confidently Extends Power For All Situations
findings.note: The 2024-11-29 announcement covers the Power 1000 (not the V2): 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 kWh options, 2,400 W continuous with the pack, US price $1,169 at launch. Our arithmetic: one pack gives 1,024 + 2,048 = 3,072 Wh, so the smallest step is 2,048 Wh.

findings.label: Cycle life / max with expansion / AC output
findings.value: 3,000 cycles to 80%+; 1,056 Wh base, up to 2,112 Wh with expansion battery; 1,800 W continuous, 2,400 W surge
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000X Portable Power Station 1056Wh | 1800W
findings.note: anker.com/products/a1761 redirects here. The page names the C1000X and an unnamed expansion battery (BP1000 is not named). One pack = +1,056 Wh, the only step. The page showed 'Price Loading', so no price was taken.

findings.label: Cycle life end point
findings.source_title: Jackery vs EcoFlow vs Bluetti vs Anker 1000Wh (2026) — Off Grid Field Guide
findings.note: Off Grid Field Guide's figure. It also says Anker (to 80%) and Jackery (to 70%) 'are not directly comparable'. The 70% end point counts more cycles than an 80% one for the same cell, so 4,000@70% is not better than 4,000@80%. Not expandable.

findings.label: Total with ONE extra battery vs the advertised 5 kWh
findings.value: 2,048 Wh with one DELTA 3 pack. 5 kWh needs the 4,096 Wh DELTA Pro 3 extra battery (1,024 + 4,096 = 5,120 Wh) via an Alternator Charger XT150 Output Cable
findings.source_title: Expansion Battery Compatibility Chart: Which Add-Ons Fit Which Power Station | StormWatts
findings.note: StormWatts lists the pack sizes (DELTA 3 / DELTA 2 1,024 Wh, DELTA 2 Max 2,048 Wh, DELTA Pro 3 4,096 Wh) and the XT150 cable for the Pro 3 and 2 Max packs. BatteryRank (https://batteryrank.com/portable-power-stations/expansion-batteries, read 2026-11-08) gives a documented limit of 1 DELTA 3 pack = 2,048 Wh. The 5,120 Wh sum is my arithmetic and was not confirmed on EcoFlow's page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Normalised table footnote
findings.value: Total after one extra battery: DELTA 3 / 3 Plus 2,048 Wh; Anker C1000X 2,112 Wh; DJI Power 1000 V2 3,072 Wh. End-of-life basis: EcoFlow, Anker and DJI rate to 80%; Jackery rates to 70%
findings.note: Built from the rows above (DJI specs, Anker C1000X page, Off Grid Field Guide, StormWatts, BatteryRank, WattHourLab), all read 2026-11-08. The advertised maximums use different pack sizes and counts: EcoFlow 5 kWh = one 4,096 Wh pack; DJI 11,264 Wh = five 2,048 Wh packs.
